newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court urges heavier sentences for Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turk court urges heavier sentences for Islamists.

text.p: A Turkish appeals court on Thursday called for heavier sentences for 81 people jailed two years ago for their part in a militant Islamist riot in which dozens of people died, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.

The court in Ankara called for 42 of the Islamists, already jailed for up to 15 years, to be retried on a new charge of "trying to change the state's constitutional order through armed aggression," the agency said

The charge carries a maximum penalty of death, although Turkey has not carried out capital punishment for more than 10 years. Convicts given the death penalty usually have their sentences commuted to life imprisonment.

The Islamists were jailed in 1994 for their part in a riot the previous year in the central town of Sivas. Rioters set fire to a hotel in the town, killing 37 people. Most of the victims were writers and singers attending a cultural festival organised by the Alevi sect, a liberal branch of Islam.
Anatolian said 39 of those first sentenced to three years in jail for aiding the rioters now faced maximum sentences of 15 years.
The court that originally heard the case can appeal against Thursday's decision.
